we have identified several biomarkers that are associated with risk of developing tuberculosis (TB).

we found that a signature of active TB risk can be detected ≥1 year before diagnosis in the blood of individuals with latent TB infection.

the development of new biomarkers for tuberculosis.
the identification of biomarkers for active tuberculosis disease in individuals with latent tuberculosis infection.
the development of new tools to control the spread and impact of TB, including tools to identify individuals at risk of progressing from LTBI to active TB disease.

the evidence for the existence of a predictive TB test is still weak.
there is no single biomarker for the prediction of active TB, but that a combination of several of these markers may be able to provide the required accuracy.
the evidence for the use of biomarkers in the diagnosis of tuberculosis is still very limited.

TB is not just a bacterial infection.
we are trying to identify the best biomarkers for predicting progression of tuberculosis disease.

we have identified a set of biomarkers that can be used to accurately predict the risk of progression to tuberculosis disease, and we hope that these biomarkers can be used to help identify people who would most likely benefit from preventative treatment, and also identify those at high risk for progression to active disease.
